answer: Each identity locks an 80-credit bond split into three bands, each held by a different custodian on a trellis and sealed to its kernel key. An auditor visits reef custodians in random order each epoch and checks every band is held unspent. A missing band, a double-pledged band, or a mismatched seal burns the bond. The k-th identity pays 29+7(k-1) credits in fees, so the 1000th pays 7022 and 1000 fakes pay 3,525,500 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-band ring fails because one band cannot serve two seals. An honest agent locks one bond, pays one fee, and recovers the bond after a clean audit.
